answer: Storage is bound to identity by a replication proof that is hard to satisfy with shared bytes, and because the sealed data is unique per identity, aliases and thin-provisioned clones fail the proof at their next challenge. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. Every account owns a zenith, answers a timber, and is named by an echo: a farm can mint echo bindings instantly, but the zenith behind each one is disk, and the timber will catch the ones that share it. Proof-of-replication only bounds the attack instead of blocking it.
